'''Aidenjin'' * {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} * {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} * {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} '''Gods in the temple''' * {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanagi}}, {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanami}} * {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=Dainaohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}}, {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=O-Naohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}} * {{ill|lt=Omoikane|Q586088|WD=Q586088|lt=Tenshikane Okami|1=Omoikane}} * {{ill|lt=Toshigami|Q3028663|WD=Q3028663|lt=Ootoshi Okami|1=Toshigami}}, {{ill|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Kurainatama Okami|1=Ukanomitama}} * {{ill|lt=Kagutsuchi|Q1640658|WD=Q1640658|lt=Kenbutsuchi Okami|1=Kagu-tsuchi}} * {{ill|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|Q2564508|WD=Q2564508|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|1=Ame-no-Koyane}} * {{ill|lt=Kyotsu deity|Q1107286|WD=Q1107286|1=Futsunushi}} === History === [[File:Hongusan.JPG|thumb|right|Motomiyayama]] === Founding === According to ``Oita Gunshi,'' {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} visited Mt. Nishikanta (currently {{ill|lt=Mt. Hongu (Oita Prefecture)|Q11520121|WD=Q11520121|lt=Mt. Hongu|1=Mount Hongū}}) on her way back from {{ill|lt=Sankan Conquest|Q11249435|WD=Q11249435|1=Three Han Campaign}} and planted a white flag on the mountaintop as proof of her visit. The local people revered it and tied a fence around it to worship it. Later, in April 1999, {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} built a shrine on Mt. Hongu, which is said to be the founding shrine. . From this tradition, it is believed that Mt. Hongu was established as {{ill|lt=Shintaiyama|Q1595289|WD=Q1595289|1=Sacred mountains}}. . === Outline === The first look at {{ill|lt=Rokukokushi|Q1151168|WD=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi|1=Rikkokushi}} is from ``{{ill|lt=Jihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'' {{ill|lt=Jōkan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}}11 ({{ill|lt=869|Q23917|WD=Q23917|1=869}}) This is an article dated March 22, which states that Nishikanta-jin is bestowed with the rank of Junior Fifth Rank and Lower. In "{{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448|1=Engishiki}}" {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, it is described as ``Nishikata Shrine'' in {{ill|lt=Bungo Province|Q864148|WD=Q864148|1=Bungo Province}}{{ill|lt=Oita District|Q8081521|WD=Q8081521|1=Ōita District, Ōita}}, making it the only major shrine in Bungo Province. It is also said to have been revered as Bungo Province {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}}. Although it declined after the late {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}}, it was revered by the feudal lord {{ill|lt=Otomo clan|Q1096662|WD=Q1096662|1=Ōtomo clan}} from the medieval period onwards. May 14th, {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}4 ({{ill|lt=1871|Q7746|WD=Q7746|1=1871}}), {{ill|lt=Modern Company Ranking System|Q712534|WD=Q712534|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} It was ranked as {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and after World War II, it became {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shrine Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === God level === * {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan|1=Jōgan}}February 15, 12 years ({{ill|lt=870 years|Q23629|WD=Q23629|1=870}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank (``{{ill|lt=Japan Sandai Jiroki|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'') === Historical evidence === ==== Formula internal ratio ==== Another non-sha of Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine, Oita District, Bungo Province'' is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishikata Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} (Usuki City, Oita Prefecture). In "Bungo no Kunishi" and "Dazai Kannaishi", it is said that this is the main shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Chikayo Otomo|Q11433259|WD=Q11433259|1=Ōtomo Chikayo}} was moved to the current location in March 15th year ({{ill|lt=1408|Q6138|WD=Q6138|1=1408}}). On the other hand, there is a strong opinion that this is the main shrine due to the area of ​​Oita County and the folklore of Mt. Hongu . ==== Specification of Ichinomiya, Bungo Province ==== Our comparison to Ichinomiya is based on such as "Bungo kokushi", "Dazai Kannaishi", "Oita gunshi", etc. On the other hand, Ichinomiya in Bungo Province also claims {{ill|lt=Yuseihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}}. There is a historical document from the year 3 ({{ill|lt=Kao|Q1150842|WD=Q1150842|1=Kaō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1171|Q19685|WD=Q19685|1=1171}}) that refers to "Yuhara Hachimangu Shrine" as Ichinomiya. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usa Hachimangu Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}There is a strong view that the separate shrine, Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, was converted into an Ichinomiya Shrine instead of our company. 48. {{Sfn|Uninomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=598}}. Although the basis for writing about Ichinomiya is unknown, the ``Shokoku Ichinomiya Jinmyo Cho'' (established before 1375) mentions Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, and the ``{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}'' (established around the 16th century) mentions our company ``Historical Development of the Medieval Ichinomiya System Volume 2'' (Iwata Shoin) p. 367. . In connection with this, the {{ill|lt=Engi|Q522046|WD=Q522046|1=Pratītyasamutpāda}} of the 10th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}} ({{ill|lt=1781|Q7719|WD=Q7719|1=1781}}) includes a tradition that ``Our company is also called Yusuhara Shrine'' and considers the two shrines to be the same . However, this is seen as a mistake. === Precincts === === Shrine building === The shrine that stands to the right of the main shrine was built in 1886. {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}}'s {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q2875112|WD=Q2875112|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=Azekura-zukuri}}. It has been designated as a cultural property of Oita City. File:Sasamuta-jinja honden.JPG|Main shrine File:Sasamuta-jinja shaden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Sasamuta-jinja shinko.JPG|Shinko (city-designated cultural property) File:Sasamuta-jinja kaguraden.JPG|Kaguraden === Mannenbashi Bridge === [[File:Sasamuta-jinja Mannen-bashi.JPG|thumb|right|Mannen Bridge (prefectural designated cultural property)]] ``Mannenbashi'' (Mannenbashi) is a stone single-arch bridge that spans the {{ill|lt=Oita River|Q11432686|WD=Q11432686|1=Ōita-gawa}} water system Samuta River (commonly known as the Misogi River), which flows through the entrance of Nishikanta Shrine. It was designated as a {{ill|lt=tangible cultural property|Q2901860|WD=Q2901860|1=Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)}} by Oita Prefecture on April 8, 1955 ({{ill|lt=1980|Q2439|WD=Q2439|1=1980}}). Not only is the main structure an arch, but the road surface also forms a gentle arc, and the stonework between the road surface and the arch is narrow. At the end of the {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}}, in {{ill|lt=Bunkyu|Q730266|WD=Q730266|1=Bunkyū}}2 ({{ill|lt=1862|Q7698|WD=Q7698|1=1862}}), jalink|Nobeoka Domain|Q10863441}} was founded by the village headman of Samuta Village, which was the territory of {{ill|lt=Oka Domain|Q8192275|WD=Q8192275|1=Oka Domain}}, {{ill|lt=Ono County] (Oita Prefecture)|Q8081661|WD=Q8081661|lt=Ono District|1=Ōno District, Ōita}} It was completed in the same year by 20 people, including Gobei Goto, the second generation stone mason from Shibakita Village (currently {{ill|lt=Bungo Ono City|Q850366|WD=Q850366|1=Bungo-Ōno}} Shibakita, Inukai Town). '''Specifications''' * Location: Samuta, Oita City, Oita Prefecture * River: Oita River system Samuda River * Format: Stone single arch bridge * Bridge length: 22.0 meters * Bridge width: 3.7 meters *Span: 11 meters * Katsuya (arch height): 3.9 meters * Completion: Bunkyu 2 (1862)* Stonemason: Gobei Goto (2nd generation) * Cultural property designation, etc.: Oita Prefecture designated tangible cultural property === Setsusha === === Okumiya === [[File:Oita hongu jinja.jpg|thumb|right|Hongu Shrine (Okumiya)]] * Hongu Shrine ** Location: Motomiya Summit ({{Coord|33|08|45.56|N|131|35|34.34|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|name=Okumiya: Hongu Shrine}}) - About 2 hours one way from the main shrine grounds. *: This is the place where our company was founded. === Precinct Company === * Merged company * Itsukushima Shrine *Kiseisha * Isesha File:Gappei-sha (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Merger company File:Itsukushima-jinja (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Itsukushima Shrine === Main festivals === === Shikinen Festival === * '''Okamiso Festival'' (Kanmiso Festival) *: Special ritual. It is held on the day of the annual festival every 33rd year. The ceremony, which is the annual grand festival in which the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine clothing|1=UNKNOWN}} of the enshrined deity is newly made and presented, is based on the history book. . * '''Shinko Taisai'''' (Goshinko Festival) *: Held every third year. === Annual festival === *Monthly festival (1st day of every month) * New Year's Day Festival (January 1st) * Harvest Star Festival (February 1st-3rd) * Prayer Festival (March 15th) * Hongu Spring Festival (March 20th) * Annual festival (April 15th) * Fuji Festival (May 3rd-5th) *: The {{ill|lt=Fuji (plant)|Q1329209|WD=Q1329209|lt=Fuji|1=Wisteria floribunda}} flowers near Mannen Bridge are at their peak. Temple festivals, tree growing festivals, memorial services, water god festivals, and Kangaku festivals are held. * Great Purification (June 30th) * Summer festival (last Sunday of July) * Hongu Autumn Festival (October 20th) * Niinamesai (November 23rd) * Great Purification, New Year's Eve Festival, Komori Fuda Burning Festival (December 31st) === Cultural assets === === Cultural property designated by Oita Prefecture === * Mannenbashi Bridge (Tangible Cultural Property) - Designated on April 8, 1982. === Cultural property designated by Oita City === [[File:Sasamuta-jinja Fuji.JPG|thumb|right|Yama Fuji (city natural monument)]] * Jinko (tangible cultural property) - Designated on January 9, 1972. * {{ill|lt=Yamafuji|Q5783537|WD=Q5783537|1=Wisteria brachybotrys}} (natural monument) - Over 450 years old, tree height 3.5m, trunk circumference 2.8m[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1219359740812/index.html List of Oita City designated famous trees (tree section)] Oita City[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1166682381846/index.html Oita City designated famous trees No. 12, 13, 14] Oita City Children's Page. Designated on January 9, 1972 [http://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1275373722750/index.html List of cultural properties designated by country, prefecture, and city] Oita City. It is also designated as a famous tree designated by Oita City (tree category). === Others === * Nishikanta Shrine Forest - Specially protected forest designated by Oita Prefecture, Oita City designated famous tree (forest section) [https://www.pref.oita.jp/soshiki/16210/hogojurin.html#8 List of specially protected forests] Oita Prefecture. === Transportation access === * Bus: Take the {{ill|lt=Oita Bus|Q11432629|WD=Q11432629|1=Oita Bus}} (bound for Fujigaoka) and get off at the "Fujigaoka Minami" bus stop. ({{Wiki coordinates|33|10|34.00|N|131|35|46.04|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|location|name=Reference: Nearest bus stop "Fujigaoka Minami"}}, about 8 minutes walk after getting off) * Railway: {{ill|lt=Kyushu Railway|Q498366|WD=Q498366|lt=JR Kyushu|1=Kyushu Railway Company}}{{ill|lt=Hohi Main Line|Q870826|WD=Q870826|1=Hōhi Main Line}} {{ill|lt=Shikito Station|Q7496590|WD=Q7496590|1=Shikido Station}} (about 30 minutes walk) === Footnotes === === Notes === {{Reflist|group="Note"}} === Source === {{Reflist|2}} === References === * Shrine history book * "Japanese Historical Place Name System Oita Prefecture Place Names" ({{ill|lt=Heibonsha|Q11482108|WD=Q11482108|1=Heibonsha}}) Oita City Nishikanta Shrine section * Masahiro Hata "Nishikata Shrine" ({{ill|lt=Kenichi Tanigawa|Q2392596|WD=Q2392596|1=Ken'ichi Tanigawa}} ed. "Japanese Gods -Shrines and Sacred Sites- 1 Kyushu" ({{ill|lt=Hakusuisha|Q4346470|WD=Q4346470|1=Hakusuisha Publishing}})) * {{Cite book|Japanese book|editor=Edited by the Medieval Countries Ichinomiya System Study Group|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries|publisher=Iwata Shoin|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|Medieval Countries Ichinomiya System|2000}}}} === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 31 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, p. 157 === Related items === * {{ill|lt=Yusihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}} - Bungo Province Ichinomiya Shrine confirmed in historical materials. *Nishikata Shrine - Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine'' Ronsha. === External link === {{commonscat|Sasamuta-jinja}} * [https://sasamuta.com/ Nishikanta Shrine] Official website * [http://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=53425 Nishikanta Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program “Shinto/Shrine Historical Materials Collection”) {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sasamuta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sasamuta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Bungo Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:大分県の神社]] [[Category:大分市の歴史]] [[Category:大分市の建築物]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:豊後国の式内社|大ささむたしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:大分県指定有形文化財]] [[Category:豊後国|社1]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]]

'''Aidenjin'' * {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} * {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} * {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} '''Gods in the temple''' * {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanagi}}, {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanami}} * {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=Dainaohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}}, {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=O-Naohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}} * {{ill|lt=Omoikane|Q586088|WD=Q586088|lt=Tenshikane Okami|1=Omoikane}} * {{ill|lt=Toshigami|Q3028663|WD=Q3028663|lt=Ootoshi Okami|1=Toshigami}}, {{ill|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Kurainatama Okami|1=Ukanomitama}} * {{ill|lt=Kagutsuchi|Q1640658|WD=Q1640658|lt=Kenbutsuchi Okami|1=Kagu-tsuchi}} * {{ill|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|Q2564508|WD=Q2564508|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|1=Ame-no-Koyane}} * {{ill|lt=Kyotsu deity|Q1107286|WD=Q1107286|1=Futsunushi}} === History === [[File:Hongusan.JPG|thumb|right|Motomiyayama]] === Founding === According to ``Oita Gunshi,'' {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} visited Mt. Nishikanta (currently {{ill|lt=Mt. Hongu (Oita Prefecture)|Q11520121|WD=Q11520121|lt=Mt. Hongu|1=Mount Hongū}}) on her way back from {{ill|lt=Sankan Conquest|Q11249435|WD=Q11249435|1=Three Han Campaign}} and planted a white flag on the mountaintop as proof of her visit. The local people revered it and tied a fence around it to worship it. Later, in April 1999, {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} built a shrine on Mt. Hongu, which is said to be the founding shrine. . From this tradition, it is believed that Mt. Hongu was established as {{ill|lt=Shintaiyama|Q1595289|WD=Q1595289|1=Sacred mountains}}. . === Outline === The first look at {{ill|lt=Rokukokushi|Q1151168|WD=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi|1=Rikkokushi}} is from ``{{ill|lt=Jihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'' {{ill|lt=Jōkan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}}11 ({{ill|lt=869|Q23917|WD=Q23917|1=869}}) This is an article dated March 22, which states that Nishikanta-jin is bestowed with the rank of Junior Fifth Rank and Lower. In "{{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448|1=Engishiki}}" {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, it is described as ``Nishikata Shrine'' in {{ill|lt=Bungo Province|Q864148|WD=Q864148|1=Bungo Province}}{{ill|lt=Oita District|Q8081521|WD=Q8081521|1=Ōita District, Ōita}}, making it the only major shrine in Bungo Province. It is also said to have been revered as Bungo Province {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}}. Although it declined after the late {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}}, it was revered by the feudal lord {{ill|lt=Otomo clan|Q1096662|WD=Q1096662|1=Ōtomo clan}} from the medieval period onwards. May 14th, {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}4 ({{ill|lt=1871|Q7746|WD=Q7746|1=1871}}), {{ill|lt=Modern Company Ranking System|Q712534|WD=Q712534|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} It was ranked as {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and after World War II, it became {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shrine Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === God level === * {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan|1=Jōgan}}February 15, 12 years ({{ill|lt=870 years|Q23629|WD=Q23629|1=870}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank (``{{ill|lt=Japan Sandai Jiroki|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'') === Historical evidence === ==== Formula internal ratio ==== Another non-sha of Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine, Oita District, Bungo Province'' is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishikata Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} (Usuki City, Oita Prefecture). In "Bungo no Kunishi" and "Dazai Kannaishi", it is said that this is the main shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Chikayo Otomo|Q11433259|WD=Q11433259|1=Ōtomo Chikayo}} was moved to the current location in March 15th year ({{ill|lt=1408|Q6138|WD=Q6138|1=1408}}). On the other hand, there is a strong opinion that this is the main shrine due to the area of ​​Oita County and the folklore of Mt. Hongu . ==== Specification of Ichinomiya, Bungo Province ==== Our comparison to Ichinomiya is based on such as "Bungo kokushi", "Dazai Kannaishi", "Oita gunshi", etc. On the other hand, Ichinomiya in Bungo Province also claims {{ill|lt=Yuseihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}}. There is a historical document from the year 3 ({{ill|lt=Kao|Q1150842|WD=Q1150842|1=Kaō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1171|Q19685|WD=Q19685|1=1171}}) that refers to "Yuhara Hachimangu Shrine" as Ichinomiya. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usa Hachimangu Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}There is a strong view that the separate shrine, Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, was converted into an Ichinomiya Shrine instead of our company. 48. {{Sfn|Uninomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=598}}. Although the basis for writing about Ichinomiya is unknown, the ``Shokoku Ichinomiya Jinmyo Cho'' (established before 1375) mentions Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, and the ``{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}'' (established around the 16th century) mentions our company ``Historical Development of the Medieval Ichinomiya System Volume 2'' (Iwata Shoin) p. 367. . In connection with this, the {{ill|lt=Engi|Q522046|WD=Q522046|1=Pratītyasamutpāda}} of the 10th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}} ({{ill|lt=1781|Q7719|WD=Q7719|1=1781}}) includes a tradition that ``Our company is also called Yusuhara Shrine'' and considers the two shrines to be the same . However, this is seen as a mistake. === Precincts === === Shrine building === The shrine that stands to the right of the main shrine was built in 1886. {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}}'s {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q2875112|WD=Q2875112|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=Azekura-zukuri}}. It has been designated as a cultural property of Oita City. File:Sasamuta-jinja honden.JPG|Main shrine File:Sasamuta-jinja shaden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Sasamuta-jinja shinko.JPG|Shinko (city-designated cultural property) File:Sasamuta-jinja kaguraden.JPG|Kaguraden === Mannenbashi Bridge === [[File:Sasamuta-jinja Mannen-bashi.JPG|thumb|right|Mannen Bridge (prefectural designated cultural property)]] ``Mannenbashi'' (Mannenbashi) is a stone single-arch bridge that spans the {{ill|lt=Oita River|Q11432686|WD=Q11432686|1=Ōita-gawa}} water system Samuta River (commonly known as the Misogi River), which flows through the entrance of Nishikanta Shrine. It was designated as a {{ill|lt=tangible cultural property|Q2901860|WD=Q2901860|1=Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)}} by Oita Prefecture on April 8, 1955 ({{ill|lt=1980|Q2439|WD=Q2439|1=1980}}). Not only is the main structure an arch, but the road surface also forms a gentle arc, and the stonework between the road surface and the arch is narrow. At the end of the {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}}, in {{ill|lt=Bunkyu|Q730266|WD=Q730266|1=Bunkyū}}2 ({{ill|lt=1862|Q7698|WD=Q7698|1=1862}}), jalink|Nobeoka Domain|Q10863441}} was founded by the village headman of Samuta Village, which was the territory of {{ill|lt=Oka Domain|Q8192275|WD=Q8192275|1=Oka Domain}}, {{ill|lt=Ono County] (Oita Prefecture)|Q8081661|WD=Q8081661|lt=Ono District|1=Ōno District, Ōita}} It was completed in the same year by 20 people, including Gobei Goto, the second generation stone mason from Shibakita Village (currently {{ill|lt=Bungo Ono City|Q850366|WD=Q850366|1=Bungo-Ōno}} Shibakita, Inukai Town). '''Specifications''' * Location: Samuta, Oita City, Oita Prefecture * River: Oita River system Samuda River * Format: Stone single arch bridge * Bridge length: 22.0 meters * Bridge width: 3.7 meters *Span: 11 meters * Katsuya (arch height): 3.9 meters * Completion: Bunkyu 2 (1862)* Stonemason: Gobei Goto (2nd generation) * Cultural property designation, etc.: Oita Prefecture designated tangible cultural property === Setsusha === === Okumiya === [[File:Oita hongu jinja.jpg|thumb|right|Hongu Shrine (Okumiya)]] * Hongu Shrine ** Location: Motomiya Summit ({{Coord|33|08|45.56|N|131|35|34.34|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|name=Okumiya: Hongu Shrine}}) - About 2 hours one way from the main shrine grounds. *: This is the place where our company was founded. === Precinct Company === * Merged company * Itsukushima Shrine *Kiseisha * Isesha File:Gappei-sha (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Merger company File:Itsukushima-jinja (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Itsukushima Shrine === Main festivals === === Shikinen Festival === * '''Okamiso Festival'' (Kanmiso Festival) *: Special ritual. It is held on the day of the annual festival every 33rd year. The ceremony, which is the annual grand festival in which the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine clothing|1=UNKNOWN}} of the enshrined deity is newly made and presented, is based on the history book. . * '''Shinko Taisai'''' (Goshinko Festival) *: Held every third year. === Annual festival === *Monthly festival (1st day of every month) * New Year's Day Festival (January 1st) * Harvest Star Festival (February 1st-3rd) * Prayer Festival (March 15th) * Hongu Spring Festival (March 20th) * Annual festival (April 15th) * Fuji Festival (May 3rd-5th) *: The {{ill|lt=Fuji (plant)|Q1329209|WD=Q1329209|lt=Fuji|1=Wisteria floribunda}} flowers near Mannen Bridge are at their peak. Temple festivals, tree growing festivals, memorial services, water god festivals, and Kangaku festivals are held. * Great Purification (June 30th) * Summer festival (last Sunday of July) * Hongu Autumn Festival (October 20th) * Niinamesai (November 23rd) * Great Purification, New Year's Eve Festival, Komori Fuda Burning Festival (December 31st) === Cultural assets === === Cultural property designated by Oita Prefecture === * Mannenbashi Bridge (Tangible Cultural Property) - Designated on April 8, 1982. === Cultural property designated by Oita City === [[File:Sasamuta-jinja Fuji.JPG|thumb|right|Yama Fuji (city natural monument)]] * Jinko (tangible cultural property) - Designated on January 9, 1972. * {{ill|lt=Yamafuji|Q5783537|WD=Q5783537|1=Wisteria brachybotrys}} (natural monument) - Over 450 years old, tree height 3.5m, trunk circumference 2.8m[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1219359740812/index.html List of Oita City designated famous trees (tree section)] Oita City[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1166682381846/index.html Oita City designated famous trees No. 12, 13, 14] Oita City Children's Page. Designated on January 9, 1972 [http://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1275373722750/index.html List of cultural properties designated by country, prefecture, and city] Oita City. It is also designated as a famous tree designated by Oita City (tree category). === Others === * Nishikanta Shrine Forest - Specially protected forest designated by Oita Prefecture, Oita City designated famous tree (forest section) [https://www.pref.oita.jp/soshiki/16210/hogojurin.html#8 List of specially protected forests] Oita Prefecture. === Transportation access === * Bus: Take the {{ill|lt=Oita Bus|Q11432629|WD=Q11432629|1=Oita Bus}} (bound for Fujigaoka) and get off at the "Fujigaoka Minami" bus stop. ({{Wiki coordinates|33|10|34.00|N|131|35|46.04|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|location|name=Reference: Nearest bus stop "Fujigaoka Minami"}}, about 8 minutes walk after getting off) * Railway: {{ill|lt=Kyushu Railway|Q498366|WD=Q498366|lt=JR Kyushu|1=Kyushu Railway Company}}{{ill|lt=Hohi Main Line|Q870826|WD=Q870826|1=Hōhi Main Line}} {{ill|lt=Shikito Station|Q7496590|WD=Q7496590|1=Shikido Station}} (about 30 minutes walk) === Footnotes === === Notes === {{Reflist|group="Note"}} === Source === {{Reflist|2}} === References === * Shrine history book * "Japanese Historical Place Name System Oita Prefecture Place Names" ({{ill|lt=Heibonsha|Q11482108|WD=Q11482108|1=Heibonsha}}) Oita City Nishikanta Shrine section * Masahiro Hata "Nishikata Shrine" ({{ill|lt=Kenichi Tanigawa|Q2392596|WD=Q2392596|1=Ken'ichi Tanigawa}} ed. "Japanese Gods -Shrines and Sacred Sites- 1 Kyushu" ({{ill|lt=Hakusuisha|Q4346470|WD=Q4346470|1=Hakusuisha Publishing}})) * {{Cite book|Japanese book|editor=Edited by the Medieval Countries Ichinomiya System Study Group|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries|publisher=Iwata Shoin|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|Medieval Countries Ichinomiya System|2000}}}} === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 31 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, p. 157 === Related items === * {{ill|lt=Yusihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}} - Bungo Province Ichinomiya Shrine confirmed in historical materials. *Nishikata Shrine - Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine'' Ronsha. === External link === {{commonscat|Sasamuta-jinja}} * [https://sasamuta.com/ Nishikanta Shrine] Official website * [http://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=53425 Nishikanta Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program “Shinto/Shrine Historical Materials Collection”) {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sasamuta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sasamuta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Bungo Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:大分県の神社]] [[Category:大分市の歴史]] [[Category:大分市の建築物]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:豊後国の式内社|大ささむたしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:国幣中社]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:大分県指定有形文化財]] [[Category:豊後国|社1]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]]

Nishikanta (currently {{ill|lt=Mt. Hongu (Oita Prefecture)|Q11520121|WD=Q11520121|lt=Mt. Hongu|1=Mount Hongū}}) on her way back from {{ill|lt=Sankan Conquest|Q11249435|WD=Q11249435|1=Three Han Campaign}} and planted a white flag on the mountaintop as proof of her visit. The local people revered it and tied a fence around it to worship it. Later, in April 1999, {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} built a shrine on Mt. Hongu, which is said to be the founding shrine. . From this tradition, it is believed that Mt. Hongu was established as {{ill|lt=Shintaiyama|Q1595289|WD=Q1595289|1=Sacred mountains}}. . === Outline === The first look at {{ill|lt=Rokukokushi|Q1151168|WD=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi|1=Rikkokushi}} is from ``{{ill|lt=Jihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'' {{ill|lt=Jōkan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}}11 ({{ill|lt=869|Q23917|WD=Q23917|1=869}}) This is an article dated March 22, which states that Nishikanta-jin is bestowed with the rank of Junior Fifth Rank and Lower. In "{{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448|1=Engishiki}}" {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, it is described as ``Nishikata Shrine'' in {{ill|lt=Bungo Province|Q864148|WD=Q864148|1=Bungo Province}}{{ill|lt=Oita District|Q8081521|WD=Q8081521|1=Ōita District, Ōita}}, making it the only major shrine in Bungo Province. It is also said to have been revered as Bungo Province {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}}. Although it declined after the late {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}}, it was revered by the feudal lord {{ill|lt=Otomo clan|Q1096662|WD=Q1096662|1=Ōtomo clan}} from the medieval period onwards. May 14th, {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}4 ({{ill|lt=1871|Q7746|WD=Q7746|1=1871}}), {{ill|lt=Modern Company Ranking System|Q712534|WD=Q712534|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} It was ranked as {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and after World War II, it became {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shrine Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === God level === * {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan|1=Jōgan}}February 15, 12 years ({{ill|lt=870 years|Q23629|WD=Q23629|1=870}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank (``{{ill|lt=Japan Sandai Jiroki|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'') === Historical evidence === ==== Formula internal ratio ==== Another non-sha of Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine, Oita District, Bungo Province'' is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishikata Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} (Usuki City, Oita Prefecture). In "Bungo no Kunishi" and "Dazai Kannaishi", it is said that this is the main shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Chikayo Otomo|Q11433259|WD=Q11433259|1=Ōtomo Chikayo}} was moved to the current location in March 15th year ({{ill|lt=1408|Q6138|WD=Q6138|1=1408}}). On the other hand, there is a strong opinion that this is the main shrine due to the area of ​​Oita County and the folklore of Mt. Hongu . ==== Specification of Ichinomiya, Bungo Province ==== Our comparison to Ichinomiya is based on such as "Bungo kokushi", "Dazai Kannaishi", "Oita gunshi", etc. On the other hand, Ichinomiya in Bungo Province also claims {{ill|lt=Yuseihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}}. There is a historical document from the year 3 ({{ill|lt=Kao|Q1150842|WD=Q1150842|1=Kaō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1171|Q19685|WD=Q19685|1=1171}}) that refers to "Yuhara Hachimangu Shrine" as Ichinomiya. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usa Hachimangu Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}There is a strong view that the separate shrine, Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, was converted into an Ichinomiya Shrine instead of our company. 48. {{Sfn|Uninomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=598}}. Although the basis for writing about Ichinomiya is unknown, the ``Shokoku Ichinomiya Jinmyo Cho'' (established before 1375) mentions Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, and the ``{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}'' (established around the 16th century) mentions our company ``Historical Development of the Medieval Ichinomiya System Volume 2'' (Iwata Shoin) p. 367. . In connection with this, the {{ill|lt=Engi|Q522046|WD=Q522046|1=Pratītyasamutpāda}} of the 10th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}} ({{ill|lt=1781|Q7719|WD=Q7719|1=1781}}) includes a tradition that ``Our company is also called Yusuhara Shrine'' and considers the two shrines to be the same . However, this is seen as a mistake. === Precincts === === Shrine building === The shrine that stands to the right of the main shrine was built in 1886. {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}}'s {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q2875112|WD=Q2875112|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=Azekura-zukuri}}. It has been designated as a cultural property of Oita City. File:Sasamuta-jinja honden.JPG|Main shrine File:Sasamuta-jinja shaden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Sasamuta-jinja shinko.JPG|Shinko (city-designated cultural property) File:Sasamuta-jinja kaguraden.JPG|Kaguraden === Mannenbashi Bridge === [[File:Sasamuta-jinja Mannen-bashi.JPG|thumb|right|Mannen Bridge (prefectural designated cultural property)]] ``Mannenbashi'' (Mannenbashi) is a stone single-arch bridge that spans the {{ill|lt=Oita River|Q11432686|WD=Q11432686|1=Ōita-gawa}} water system Samuta River (commonly known as the Misogi River), which flows through the entrance of Nishikanta Shrine. It was designated as a {{ill|lt=tangible cultural property|Q2901860|WD=Q2901860|1=Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)}} by Oita Prefecture on April 8, 1955 ({{ill|lt=1980|Q2439|WD=Q2439|1=1980}}). Not only is the main structure an arch, but the road surface also forms a gentle arc, and the stonework between the road surface and the arch is narrow. At the end of the {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}}, in {{ill|lt=Bunkyu|Q730266|WD=Q730266|1=Bunkyū}}2 ({{ill|lt=1862|Q7698|WD=Q7698|1=1862}}), jalink|Nobeoka Domain|Q10863441}} was founded by the village headman of Samuta Village, which was the territory of {{ill|lt=Oka Domain|Q8192275|WD=Q8192275|1=Oka Domain}}, {{ill|lt=Ono County] (Oita Prefecture)|Q8081661|WD=Q8081661|lt=Ono District|1=Ōno District, Ōita}} It was completed in the same year by 20 people, including Gobei Goto, the second generation stone mason from Shibakita Village (currently {{ill|lt=Bungo Ono City|Q850366|WD=Q850366|1=Bungo-Ōno}} Shibakita, Inukai Town). '''Specifications''' * Location: Samuta, Oita City, Oita Prefecture * River: Oita River system Samuda River * Format: Stone single arch bridge * Bridge length: 22.0 meters * Bridge width: 3.7 meters *Span: 11 meters * Katsuya (arch height): 3.9 meters * Completion: Bunkyu 2 (1862)* Stonemason: Gobei Goto (2nd generation) * Cultural property designation, etc.: Oita Prefecture designated tangible cultural property === Setsusha === === Okumiya === [[File:Oita hongu jinja.jpg|thumb|right|Hongu Shrine (Okumiya)]] * Hongu Shrine ** Location: Motomiya Summit ({{Coord|33|08|45.56|N|131|35|34.34|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|name=Okumiya: Hongu Shrine}}) - About 2 hours one way from the main shrine grounds. *: This is the place where our company was founded. === Precinct Company === * Merged company * Itsukushima Shrine *Kiseisha * Isesha File:Gappei-sha (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Merger company File:Itsukushima-jinja (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Itsukushima Shrine === Main festivals === === Shikinen Festival === * '''Okamiso Festival'' (Kanmiso Festival) *: Special ritual. It is held on the day of the annual festival every 33rd year. The ceremony, which is the annual grand festival in which the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine clothing|1=UNKNOWN}} of the enshrined deity is newly made and presented, is based on the history book. . * '''Shinko Taisai'''' (Goshinko Festival) *: Held every third year. === Annual festival === *Monthly festival (1st day of every month) * New Year's Day Festival (January 1st) * Harvest Star Festival (February 1st-3rd) * Prayer Festival (March 15th) * Hongu Spring Festival (March 20th) * Annual festival (April 15th) * Fuji Festival (May 3rd-5th) *: The {{ill|lt=Fuji (plant)|Q1329209|WD=Q1329209|lt=Fuji|1=Wisteria floribunda}} flowers near Mannen Bridge are at their peak. Temple festivals, tree growing festivals, memorial services, water god festivals, and Kangaku festivals are held. * Great Purification (June 30th) * Summer festival (last Sunday of July) * Hongu Autumn Festival (October 20th) * Niinamesai (November 23rd) * Great Purification, New Year's Eve Festival, Komori Fuda Burning Festival (December 31st) === Cultural assets === === Cultural property designated by Oita Prefecture === * Mannenbashi Bridge (Tangible Cultural Property) - Designated on April 8, 1982. === Cultural property designated by Oita City === [[File:Sasamuta-jinja Fuji.JPG|thumb|right|Yama Fuji (city natural monument)]] * Jinko (tangible cultural property) - Designated on January 9, 1972. * {{ill|lt=Yamafuji|Q5783537|WD=Q5783537|1=Wisteria brachybotrys}} (natural monument) - Over 450 years old, tree height 3.5m, trunk circumference 2.8m[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1219359740812/index.html List of Oita City designated famous trees (tree section)] Oita City[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1166682381846/index.html Oita City designated famous trees No. 12, 13, 14] Oita City Children's Page. Designated on January 9, 1972 [http://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1275373722750/index.html List of cultural properties designated by country, prefecture, and city] Oita City. It is also designated as a famous tree designated by Oita City (tree category). === Others === * Nishikanta Shrine Forest - Specially protected forest designated by Oita Prefecture, Oita City designated famous tree (forest section) [https://www.pref.oita.jp/soshiki/16210/hogojurin.html#8 List of specially protected forests] Oita Prefecture. === Transportation access === * Bus: Take the {{ill|lt=Oita Bus|Q11432629|WD=Q11432629|1=Oita Bus}} (bound for Fujigaoka) and get off at the "Fujigaoka Minami" bus stop. ({{Wiki coordinates|33|10|34.00|N|131|35|46.04|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|location|name=Reference: Nearest bus stop "Fujigaoka Minami"}}, about 8 minutes walk after getting off) * Railway: {{ill|lt=Kyushu Railway|Q498366|WD=Q498366|lt=JR Kyushu|1=Kyushu Railway Company}}{{ill|lt=Hohi Main Line|Q870826|WD=Q870826|1=Hōhi Main Line}} {{ill|lt=Shikito Station|Q7496590|WD=Q7496590|1=Shikido Station}} (about 30 minutes walk) === Footnotes === === Notes === {{Reflist|group="Note"}} === Source === {{Reflist|2}} === References === * Shrine history book * "Japanese Historical Place Name System Oita Prefecture Place Names" ({{ill|lt=Heibonsha|Q11482108|WD=Q11482108|1=Heibonsha}}) Oita City Nishikanta Shrine section * Masahiro Hata "Nishikata Shrine" ({{ill|lt=Kenichi Tanigawa|Q2392596|WD=Q2392596|1=Ken'ichi Tanigawa}} ed. "Japanese Gods -Shrines and Sacred Sites- 1 Kyushu" ({{ill|lt=Hakusuisha|Q4346470|WD=Q4346470|1=Hakusuisha Publishing}})) * {{Cite book|Japanese book|editor=Edited by the Medieval Countries Ichinomiya System Study Group|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries|publisher=Iwata Shoin|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|Medieval Countries Ichinomiya System|2000}}}} === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 31 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, p. 157 === Related items === * {{ill|lt=Yusihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}} - Bungo Province Ichinomiya Shrine confirmed in historical materials. *Nishikata Shrine - Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine'' Ronsha. === External link === {{commonscat|Sasamuta-jinja}} * [https://sasamuta.com/ Nishikanta Shrine] Official website * [http://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=53425 Nishikanta Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program “Shinto/Shrine Historical Materials Collection”) {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sasamuta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sasamuta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Bungo Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:大分県の神社]] [[Category:大分市の歴史]] [[Category:大分市の建築物]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:豊後国の式内社|大ささむたしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:大分県指定有形文化財]] [[Category:豊後国|社1]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]]

'''Aidenjin'' * {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} * {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} * {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} '''Gods in the temple''' * {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanagi}}, {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanami}} * {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=Dainaohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}}, {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=O-Naohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}} * {{ill|lt=Omoikane|Q586088|WD=Q586088|lt=Tenshikane Okami|1=Omoikane}} * {{ill|lt=Toshigami|Q3028663|WD=Q3028663|lt=Ootoshi Okami|1=Toshigami}}, {{ill|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Kurainatama Okami|1=Ukanomitama}} * {{ill|lt=Kagutsuchi|Q1640658|WD=Q1640658|lt=Kenbutsuchi Okami|1=Kagu-tsuchi}} * {{ill|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|Q2564508|WD=Q2564508|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|1=Ame-no-Koyane}} * {{ill|lt=Kyotsu deity|Q1107286|WD=Q1107286|1=Futsunushi}} === History === [[File:Hongusan.JPG|thumb|right|Motomiyayama]] === Founding === According to ``Oita Gunshi,'' {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} visited Mt. Nishikanta (currently {{ill|lt=Mt. Hongu (Oita Prefecture)|Q11520121|WD=Q11520121|lt=Mt. Hongu|1=Mount Hongū}}) on her way back from {{ill|lt=Sankan Conquest|Q11249435|WD=Q11249435|1=Three Han Campaign}} and planted a white flag on the mountaintop as proof of her visit. The local people revered it and tied a fence around it to worship it. Later, in April 1999, {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} built a shrine on Mt. Hongu, which is said to be the founding shrine. . From this tradition, it is believed that Mt. Hongu was established as {{ill|lt=Shintaiyama|Q1595289|WD=Q1595289|1=Sacred mountains}}. . === Outline === The first look at {{ill|lt=Rokukokushi|Q1151168|WD=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi|1=Rikkokushi}} is from ``{{ill|lt=Jihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'' {{ill|lt=Jōkan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}}11 ({{ill|lt=869|Q23917|WD=Q23917|1=869}}) This is an article dated March 22, which states that Nishikanta-jin is bestowed with the rank of Junior Fifth Rank and Lower. In "{{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448|1=Engishiki}}" {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, it is described as ``Nishikata Shrine'' in {{ill|lt=Bungo Province|Q864148|WD=Q864148|1=Bungo Province}}{{ill|lt=Oita District|Q8081521|WD=Q8081521|1=Ōita District, Ōita}}, making it the only major shrine in Bungo Province. It is also said to have been revered as Bungo Province {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}}. Although it declined after the late {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}}, it was revered by the feudal lord {{ill|lt=Otomo clan|Q1096662|WD=Q1096662|1=Ōtomo clan}} from the medieval period onwards. May 14th, {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}4 ({{ill|lt=1871|Q7746|WD=Q7746|1=1871}}), {{ill|lt=Modern Company Ranking System|Q712534|WD=Q712534|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} It was ranked as {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and after World War II, it became {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shrine Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === God level === * {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan|1=Jōgan}}February 15, 12 years ({{ill|lt=870 years|Q23629|WD=Q23629|1=870}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank (``{{ill|lt=Japan Sandai Jiroki|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'') === Historical evidence === ==== Formula internal ratio ==== Another non-sha of Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine, Oita District, Bungo Province'' is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishikata Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} (Usuki City, Oita Prefecture). In "Bungo no Kunishi" and "Dazai Kannaishi", it is said that this is the main shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Chikayo Otomo|Q11433259|WD=Q11433259|1=Ōtomo Chikayo}} was moved to the current location in March 15th year ({{ill|lt=1408|Q6138|WD=Q6138|1=1408}}). On the other hand, there is a strong opinion that this is the main shrine due to the area of ​​Oita County and the folklore of Mt. Hongu . ==== Specification of Ichinomiya, Bungo Province ==== Our comparison to Ichinomiya is based on such as "Bungo kokushi", "Dazai Kannaishi", "Oita gunshi", etc. On the other hand, Ichinomiya in Bungo Province also claims {{ill|lt=Yuseihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}}. There is a historical document from the year 3 ({{ill|lt=Kao|Q1150842|WD=Q1150842|1=Kaō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1171|Q19685|WD=Q19685|1=1171}}) that refers to "Yuhara Hachimangu Shrine" as Ichinomiya. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usa Hachimangu Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}There is a strong view that the separate shrine, Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, was converted into an Ichinomiya Shrine instead of our company. 48. {{Sfn|Uninomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=598}}. Although the basis for writing about Ichinomiya is unknown, the ``Shokoku Ichinomiya Jinmyo Cho'' (established before 1375) mentions Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, and the ``{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}'' (established around the 16th century) mentions our company ``Historical Development of the Medieval Ichinomiya System Volume 2'' (Iwata Shoin) p. 367. . In connection with this, the {{ill|lt=Engi|Q522046|WD=Q522046|1=Pratītyasamutpāda}} of the 10th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}} ({{ill|lt=1781|Q7719|WD=Q7719|1=1781}}) includes a tradition that ``Our company is also called Yusuhara Shrine'' and considers the two shrines to be the same . However, this is seen as a mistake. === Precincts === === Shrine building === The shrine that stands to the right of the main shrine was built in 1886. {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}}'s {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q2875112|WD=Q2875112|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=Azekura-zukuri}}. It has been designated as a cultural property of Oita City. It was designated as a {{ill|lt=tangible cultural property|Q2901860|WD=Q2901860|1=Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)}} by Oita Prefecture on April 8, 1955 ({{ill|lt=1980|Q2439|WD=Q2439|1=1980}}). Not only is the main structure an arch, but the road surface also forms a gentle arc, and the stonework between the road surface and the arch is narrow. At the end of the {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}}, in {{ill|lt=Bunkyu|Q730266|WD=Q730266|1=Bunkyū}}2 ({{ill|lt=1862|Q7698|WD=Q7698|1=1862}}), jalink|Nobeoka Domain|Q10863441}} was founded by the village headman of Samuta Village, which was the territory of {{ill|lt=Oka Domain|Q8192275|WD=Q8192275|1=Oka Domain}}, {{ill|lt=Ono County] (Oita Prefecture)|Q8081661|WD=Q8081661|lt=Ono District|1=Ōno District, Ōita}} It was completed in the same year by 20 people, including Gobei Goto, the second generation stone mason from Shibakita Village (currently {{ill|lt=Bungo Ono City|Q850366|WD=Q850366|1=Bungo-Ōno}} Shibakita, Inukai Town). '''Specifications''' * Location: Samuta, Oita City, Oita Prefecture * River: Oita River system Samuda River * Format: Stone single arch bridge * Bridge length: 22.0 meters * Bridge width: 3.7 meters *Span: 11 meters * Katsuya (arch height): 3.9 meters * Completion: Bunkyu 2 (1862)* Stonemason: Gobei Goto (2nd generation) * Cultural property designation, etc.: Oita Prefecture designated tangible cultural property === Setsusha === === Okumiya === [[File:Oita hongu jinja.jpg|thumb|right|Hongu Shrine (Okumiya)]] * Hongu Shrine ** Location: Motomiya Summit ({{Coord|33|08|45.56|N|131|35|34.34|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|name=Okumiya: Hongu Shrine}}) - About 2 hours one way from the main shrine grounds. *: This is the place where our company was founded. === Precinct Company === * Merged company * Itsukushima Shrine *Kiseisha * Isesha File:Gappei-sha (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Merger company File:Itsukushima-jinja (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Itsukushima Shrine === Main festivals === === Shikinen Festival === * '''Okamiso Festival'' (Kanmiso Festival) *: Special ritual. It is held on the day of the annual festival every 33rd year. The ceremony, which is the annual grand festival in which the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine clothing|1=UNKNOWN}} of the enshrined deity is newly made and presented, is based on the history book. . * '''Shinko Taisai'''' (Goshinko Festival) *: Held every third year. === Annual festival === *Monthly festival (1st day of every month) * New Year's Day Festival (January 1st) * Harvest Star Festival (February 1st-3rd) * Prayer Festival (March 15th) * Hongu Spring Festival (March 20th) * Annual festival (April 15th) * Fuji Festival (May 3rd-5th) *: The {{ill|lt=Fuji (plant)|Q1329209|WD=Q1329209|lt=Fuji|1=Wisteria floribunda}} flowers near Mannen Bridge are at their peak. Temple festivals, tree growing festivals, memorial services, water god festivals, and Kangaku festivals are held. * Great Purification (June 30th) * Summer festival (last Sunday of July) * Hongu Autumn Festival (October 20th) * Niinamesai (November 23rd) * Great Purification, New Year's Eve Festival, Komori Fuda Burning Festival (December 31st) === Cultural assets === === Cultural property designated by Oita Prefecture === * Mannenbashi Bridge (Tangible Cultural Property) - Designated on April 8, 1982. === Cultural property designated by Oita City === [[File:Sasamuta-jinja Fuji.JPG|thumb|right|Yama Fuji (city natural monument)]] * Jinko (tangible cultural property) - Designated on January 9, 1972. * {{ill|lt=Yamafuji|Q5783537|WD=Q5783537|1=Wisteria brachybotrys}} (natural monument) - Over 450 years old, tree height 3.5m, trunk circumference 2.8m[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1219359740812/index.html List of Oita City designated famous trees (tree section)] Oita City[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1166682381846/index.html Oita City designated famous trees No. 12, 13, 14] Oita City Children's Page. Designated on January 9, 1972 [http://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1275373722750/index.html List of cultural properties designated by country, prefecture, and city] Oita City. It is also designated as a famous tree designated by Oita City (tree category). === Others === * Nishikanta Shrine Forest - Specially protected forest designated by Oita Prefecture, Oita City designated famous tree (forest section) [https://www.pref.oita.jp/soshiki/16210/hogojurin.html#8 List of specially protected forests] Oita Prefecture. === Transportation access === * Bus: Take the {{ill|lt=Oita Bus|Q11432629|WD=Q11432629|1=Oita Bus}} (bound for Fujigaoka) and get off at the "Fujigaoka Minami" bus stop. ({{Wiki coordinates|33|10|34.00|N|131|35|46.04|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|location|name=Reference: Nearest bus stop "Fujigaoka Minami"}}, about 8 minutes walk after getting off) * Railway: {{ill|lt=Kyushu Railway|Q498366|WD=Q498366|lt=JR Kyushu|1=Kyushu Railway Company}}{{ill|lt=Hohi Main Line|Q870826|WD=Q870826|1=Hōhi Main Line}} {{ill|lt=Shikito Station|Q7496590|WD=Q7496590|1=Shikido Station}} (about 30 minutes walk) === Footnotes === === Notes === {{Reflist|group="Note"}} === Source === {{Reflist|2}} === References === * Shrine history book * "Japanese Historical Place Name System Oita Prefecture Place Names" ({{ill|lt=Heibonsha|Q11482108|WD=Q11482108|1=Heibonsha}}) Oita City Nishikanta Shrine section * Masahiro Hata "Nishikata Shrine" ({{ill|lt=Kenichi Tanigawa|Q2392596|WD=Q2392596|1=Ken'ichi Tanigawa}} ed. '''Aidenjin'' * {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} * {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} * {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} '''Gods in the temple''' * {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanagi}}, {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanami}} * {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=Dainaohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}}, {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=O-Naohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}} * {{ill|lt=Omoikane|Q586088|WD=Q586088|lt=Tenshikane Okami|1=Omoikane}} * {{ill|lt=Toshigami|Q3028663|WD=Q3028663|lt=Ootoshi Okami|1=Toshigami}}, {{ill|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Kurainatama Okami|1=Ukanomitama}} * {{ill|lt=Kagutsuchi|Q1640658|WD=Q1640658|lt=Kenbutsuchi Okami|1=Kagu-tsuchi}} * {{ill|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|Q2564508|WD=Q2564508|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|1=Ame-no-Koyane}} * {{ill|lt=Kyotsu deity|Q1107286|WD=Q1107286|1=Futsunushi}} === History === [[File:Hongusan.JPG|thumb|right|Motomiyayama]] === Founding === According to ``Oita Gunshi,'' {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} visited Mt. Nishikanta (currently {{ill|lt=Mt. Hongu (Oita Prefecture)|Q11520121|WD=Q11520121|lt=Mt. Hongu|1=Mount Hongū}}) on her way back from {{ill|lt=Sankan Conquest|Q11249435|WD=Q11249435|1=Three Han Campaign}} and planted a white flag on the mountaintop as proof of her visit. The local people revered it and tied a fence around it to worship it. Later, in April 1999, {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} built a shrine on Mt. Hongu, which is said to be the founding shrine. . From this tradition, it is believed that Mt. Hongu was established as {{ill|lt=Shintaiyama|Q1595289|WD=Q1595289|1=Sacred mountains}}. . === Outline === The first look at {{ill|lt=Rokukokushi|Q1151168|WD=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi|1=Rikkokushi}} is from ``{{ill|lt=Jihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'' {{ill|lt=Jōkan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}}11 ({{ill|lt=869|Q23917|WD=Q23917|1=869}}) This is an article dated March 22, which states that Nishikanta-jin is bestowed with the rank of Junior Fifth Rank and Lower. In "{{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448|1=Engishiki}}" {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, it is described as ``Nishikata Shrine'' in {{ill|lt=Bungo Province|Q864148|WD=Q864148|1=Bungo Province}}{{ill|lt=Oita District|Q8081521|WD=Q8081521|1=Ōita District, Ōita}}, making it the only major shrine in Bungo Province. It is also said to have been revered as Bungo Province {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}}. Although it declined after the late {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}}, it was revered by the feudal lord {{ill|lt=Otomo clan|Q1096662|WD=Q1096662|1=Ōtomo clan}} from the medieval period onwards. May 14th, {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}4 ({{ill|lt=1871|Q7746|WD=Q7746|1=1871}}), {{ill|lt=Modern Company Ranking System|Q712534|WD=Q712534|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} It was ranked as {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and after World War II, it became {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shrine Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === God level === * {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan|1=Jōgan}}February 15, 12 years ({{ill|lt=870 years|Q23629|WD=Q23629|1=870}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank (``{{ill|lt=Japan Sandai Jiroki|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'') === Historical evidence === ==== Formula internal ratio ==== Another non-sha of Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine, Oita District, Bungo Province'' is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishikata Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} (Usuki City, Oita Prefecture). In "Bungo no Kunishi" and "Dazai Kannaishi", it is said that this is the main shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Chikayo Otomo|Q11433259|WD=Q11433259|1=Ōtomo Chikayo}} was moved to the current location in March 15th year ({{ill|lt=1408|Q6138|WD=Q6138|1=1408}}). On the other hand, there is a strong opinion that this is the main shrine due to the area of ​​Oita County and the folklore of Mt. Hongu . ==== Specification of Ichinomiya, Bungo Province ==== Our comparison to Ichinomiya is based on such as "Bungo kokushi", "Dazai Kannaishi", "Oita gunshi", etc. On the other hand, Ichinomiya in Bungo Province also claims {{ill|lt=Yuseihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}}. There is a historical document from the year 3 ({{ill|lt=Kao|Q1150842|WD=Q1150842|1=Kaō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1171|Q19685|WD=Q19685|1=1171}}) that refers to "Yuhara Hachimangu Shrine" as Ichinomiya. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usa Hachimangu Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}There is a strong view that the separate shrine, Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, was converted into an Ichinomiya Shrine instead of our company. 48. {{Sfn|Uninomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=598}}. Although the basis for writing about Ichinomiya is unknown, the ``Shokoku Ichinomiya Jinmyo Cho'' (established before 1375) mentions Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, and the ``{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}'' (established around the 16th century) mentions our company ``Historical Development of the Medieval Ichinomiya System Volume 2'' (Iwata Shoin) p. 367. . In connection with this, the {{ill|lt=Engi|Q522046|WD=Q522046|1=Pratītyasamutpāda}} of the 10th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}} ({{ill|lt=1781|Q7719|WD=Q7719|1=1781}}) includes a tradition that ``Our company is also called Yusuhara Shrine'' and considers the two shrines to be the same . However, this is seen as a mistake. === Precincts === === Shrine building === The shrine that stands to the right of the main shrine was built in 1886. {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}}'s {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q2875112|WD=Q2875112|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=Azekura-zukuri}}. It has been designated as a cultural property of Oita City. It was designated as a {{ill|lt=tangible cultural property|Q2901860|WD=Q2901860|1=Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)}} by Oita Prefecture on April 8, 1955 ({{ill|lt=1980|Q2439|WD=Q2439|1=1980}}). Not only is the main structure an arch, but the road surface also forms a gentle arc, and the stonework between the road surface and the arch is narrow. At the end of the {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}}, in {{ill|lt=Bunkyu|Q730266|WD=Q730266|1=Bunkyū}}2 ({{ill|lt=1862|Q7698|WD=Q7698|1=1862}}), jalink|Nobeoka Domain|Q10863441}} was founded by the village headman of Samuta Village, which was the territory of {{ill|lt=Oka Domain|Q8192275|WD=Q8192275|1=Oka Domain}}, {{ill|lt=Ono County] (Oita Prefecture)|Q8081661|WD=Q8081661|lt=Ono District|1=Ōno District, Ōita}} It was completed in the same year by 20 people, including Gobei Goto, the second generation stone mason from Shibakita Village (currently {{ill|lt=Bungo Ono City|Q850366|WD=Q850366|1=Bungo-Ōno}} Shibakita, Inukai Town). {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} |Foundation = (tradition) 15th {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}}9 years |Main shrine = |alias= |Fudasho, etc. = |Regular festival = {{ill|lt=April 15th|Q2497|WD=Q2497|1=April 15}} |Shinto ritual = Kamui Festival (once every 32 years)|Map = {{Location map|Japan Oita|label=Nishikata Shrine|position=bottom|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=10|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{List of coordinates}} [[File:Sasamuta-jinja torii.JPG|thumb|right|torii]] [[File:Sasamuta-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|right|Distant view of the precincts]] ``Sasamuta Shrine'' is located in {{ill|lt=Oita Prefecture|Q133924|WD=Q133924|1=Ōita Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=Oita City|Q199609|WD=Q199609|1=Ōita (city)}}. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinai Shrine|1=Shikinaisha|WD=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Taisha), {{ill|lt=Bungo Province|Q864148|WD=Q864148|1=Bungo Province}}{{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}}. {{ill|lt=Modern shrine rank system|Q712534|WD=Q712534|lt=old shrine rank|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and currently it is {{ill|lt=Beppyō Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shinja Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === Enshrined God === '''Main shrine (main shrine)''' * '''Sasamuta no Okami'''' (Sasamuta no Okami) *: It is a general term for {{ill|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|Q455602|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami|1=Amaterasu}}, {{ill|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|WD=Q595520|lt=Tsukiyomi-son|1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|lt=Ame no Oshihomimi|Q462555|WD=Q462555|lt=Amenohomi no Mikoto|1=Ame-no-oshihomimi}}The enshrined deities are according to the history book. . '''Aidenjin'' * {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} * {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} * {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} '''Gods in the temple''' * {{ill|lt=Izanagi|Q813858|WD=Q813858|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanagi}}, {{ill|lt=Izanami|Q682306|WD=Q682306|lt=Izanami Okami|1=Izanami}} * {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=Dainaohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}}, {{ill|lt=Naobi-kami|Q11581794|WD=Q11581794|lt=O-Naohi-no-kami|1=Ōnaobi no Kami}} * {{ill|lt=Omoikane|Q586088|WD=Q586088|lt=Tenshikane Okami|1=Omoikane}} * {{ill|lt=Toshigami|Q3028663|WD=Q3028663|lt=Ootoshi Okami|1=Toshigami}}, {{ill|WD=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|WD=Q3080728|lt=Kurainatama Okami|1=Ukanomitama}} * {{ill|lt=Kagutsuchi|Q1640658|WD=Q1640658|lt=Kenbutsuchi Okami|1=Kagu-tsuchi}} * {{ill|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|Q2564508|WD=Q2564508|lt=Amagiya Mikoto|1=Ame-no-Koyane}} * {{ill|lt=Kyotsu deity|Q1107286|WD=Q1107286|1=Futsunushi}} === History === [[File:Hongusan.JPG|thumb|right|Motomiyayama]] === Founding === According to ``Oita Gunshi,'' {{ill|lt=Empress Jingu|Q232803|WD=Q232803|1=Empress Jingū}} visited Mt. Nishikanta (currently {{ill|lt=Mt. Hongu (Oita Prefecture)|Q11520121|WD=Q11520121|lt=Mt. Hongu|1=Mount Hongū}}) on her way back from {{ill|lt=Sankan Conquest|Q11249435|WD=Q11249435|1=Three Han Campaign}} and planted a white flag on the mountaintop as proof of her visit. The local people revered it and tied a fence around it to worship it. Later, in April 1999, {{ill|lt=Emperor Ojin|Q317997|WD=Q317997|1=Emperor Ōjin}} {{ill|lt=Takeuchi Sukune|Q1073668|WD=Q1073668|1=Takenouchi no Sukune}} built a shrine on Mt. Hongu, which is said to be the founding shrine. . From this tradition, it is believed that Mt. Hongu was established as {{ill|lt=Shintaiyama|Q1595289|WD=Q1595289|1=Sacred mountains}}. . === Outline === The first look at {{ill|lt=Rokukokushi|Q1151168|WD=Q1151168|lt=Kokushi|1=Rikkokushi}} is from ``{{ill|lt=Jihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'' {{ill|lt=Jōkan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan|1=Jōgan}}11 ({{ill|lt=869|Q23917|WD=Q23917|1=869}}) This is an article dated March 22, which states that Nishikanta-jin is bestowed with the rank of Junior Fifth Rank and Lower. In "{{ill|lt=Engishiki|Q1342448|WD=Q1342448|1=Engishiki}}" {{ill|lt=Engishiki Shinmyocho|Q11064932|WD=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}, it is described as ``Nishikata Shrine'' in {{ill|lt=Bungo Province|Q864148|WD=Q864148|1=Bungo Province}}{{ill|lt=Oita District|Q8081521|WD=Q8081521|1=Ōita District, Ōita}}, making it the only major shrine in Bungo Province. It is also said to have been revered as Bungo Province {{ill|lt=Ichinomiya|Q1656379|WD=Q1656379|1=Ichinomiya}}. Although it declined after the late {{ill|lt=Heian period|Q193292|WD=Q193292|1=Heian period}}, it was revered by the feudal lord {{ill|lt=Otomo clan|Q1096662|WD=Q1096662|1=Ōtomo clan}} from the medieval period onwards. May 14th, {{ill|lt=Meiji|Q3125096|WD=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}4 ({{ill|lt=1871|Q7746|WD=Q7746|1=1871}}), {{ill|lt=Modern Company Ranking System|Q712534|WD=Q712534|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} It was ranked as {{ill|UNKNOWN|WD=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha|1=Kokuhei Chūsha}}, and after World War II, it became {{ill|lt=Beppyo Shrine|Q10898274|WD=Q10898274|1=Beppyo shrine}} of {{ill|lt=Shrine Honcho|Q908077|WD=Q908077|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}. === God level === * {{ill|lt=Jōgan (Japan)|Q1075635|WD=Q1075635|lt=Jōkan|1=Jōgan}}February 15, 12 years ({{ill|lt=870 years|Q23629|WD=Q23629|1=870}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank (``{{ill|lt=Japan Sandai Jiroki|Q1052981|WD=Q1052981|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}'') === Historical evidence === ==== Formula internal ratio ==== Another non-sha of Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine, Oita District, Bungo Province'' is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nishikata Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}} (Usuki City, Oita Prefecture). In "Bungo no Kunishi" and "Dazai Kannaishi", it is said that this is the main shrine, and it is said that {{ill|lt=Chikayo Otomo|Q11433259|WD=Q11433259|1=Ōtomo Chikayo}} was moved to the current location in March 15th year ({{ill|lt=1408|Q6138|WD=Q6138|1=1408}}). On the other hand, there is a strong opinion that this is the main shrine due to the area of ​​Oita County and the folklore of Mt. Hongu . ==== Specification of Ichinomiya, Bungo Province ==== Our comparison to Ichinomiya is based on such as "Bungo kokushi", "Dazai Kannaishi", "Oita gunshi", etc. On the other hand, Ichinomiya in Bungo Province also claims {{ill|lt=Yuseihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}}. There is a historical document from the year 3 ({{ill|lt=Kao|Q1150842|WD=Q1150842|1=Kaō (era)}} ({{ill|lt=1171|Q19685|WD=Q19685|1=1171}}) that refers to "Yuhara Hachimangu Shrine" as Ichinomiya. {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Usa Hachimangu Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}There is a strong view that the separate shrine, Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, was converted into an Ichinomiya Shrine instead of our company. 48. {{Sfn|Uninomiya system in medieval countries|2000|p=598}}. Although the basis for writing about Ichinomiya is unknown, the ``Shokoku Ichinomiya Jinmyo Cho'' (established before 1375) mentions Yusuhara Hachimangu Shrine, and the ``{{ill|lt=Dainippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki|Q11435648|WD=Q11435648|1=Dai Nippon Koku Ichinomiya Ki}}'' (established around the 16th century) mentions our company ``Historical Development of the Medieval Ichinomiya System Volume 2'' (Iwata Shoin) p. 367. . In connection with this, the {{ill|lt=Engi|Q522046|WD=Q522046|1=Pratītyasamutpāda}} of the 10th year of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yasunaga|1=UNKNOWN}} ({{ill|lt=1781|Q7719|WD=Q7719|1=1781}}) includes a tradition that ``Our company is also called Yusuhara Shrine'' and considers the two shrines to be the same . However, this is seen as a mistake. === Precincts === === Shrine building === The shrine that stands to the right of the main shrine was built in 1886. {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q855025|WD=Q855025|lt=Irimoya|1=East Asian hip-and-gable roof}}'s {{ill|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|Q2875112|WD=Q2875112|lt=Irimoya-zukuri|1=Azekura-zukuri}}. It has been designated as a cultural property of Oita City. File:Sasamuta-jinja honden.JPG|Main shrine File:Sasamuta-jinja shaden.JPG|Shrine of worship File:Sasamuta-jinja shinko.JPG|Shinko (city-designated cultural property) File:Sasamuta-jinja kaguraden.JPG|Kaguraden === Mannenbashi Bridge === [[File:Sasamuta-jinja Mannen-bashi.JPG|thumb|right|Mannen Bridge (prefectural designated cultural property)]] ``Mannenbashi'' (Mannenbashi) is a stone single-arch bridge that spans the {{ill|lt=Oita River|Q11432686|WD=Q11432686|1=Ōita-gawa}} water system Samuta River (commonly known as the Misogi River), which flows through the entrance of Nishikanta Shrine. It was designated as a {{ill|lt=tangible cultural property|Q2901860|WD=Q2901860|1=Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)}} by Oita Prefecture on April 8, 1955 ({{ill|lt=1980|Q2439|WD=Q2439|1=1980}}). Not only is the main structure an arch, but the road surface also forms a gentle arc, and the stonework between the road surface and the arch is narrow. At the end of the {{ill|lt=Edo period|Q184963|WD=Q184963|1=Edo period}}, in {{ill|lt=Bunkyu|Q730266|WD=Q730266|1=Bunkyū}}2 ({{ill|lt=1862|Q7698|WD=Q7698|1=1862}}), jalink|Nobeoka Domain|Q10863441}} was founded by the village headman of Samuta Village, which was the territory of {{ill|lt=Oka Domain|Q8192275|WD=Q8192275|1=Oka Domain}}, {{ill|lt=Ono County] (Oita Prefecture)|Q8081661|WD=Q8081661|lt=Ono District|1=Ōno District, Ōita}} It was completed in the same year by 20 people, including Gobei Goto, the second generation stone mason from Shibakita Village (currently {{ill|lt=Bungo Ono City|Q850366|WD=Q850366|1=Bungo-Ōno}} Shibakita, Inukai Town). '''Specifications''' * Location: Samuta, Oita City, Oita Prefecture * River: Oita River system Samuda River * Format: Stone single arch bridge * Bridge length: 22.0 meters * Bridge width: 3.7 meters *Span: 11 meters * Katsuya (arch height): 3.9 meters * Completion: Bunkyu 2 (1862)* Stonemason: Gobei Goto (2nd generation) * Cultural property designation, etc.: Oita Prefecture designated tangible cultural property === Setsusha === === Okumiya === [[File:Oita hongu jinja.jpg|thumb|right|Hongu Shrine (Okumiya)]] * Hongu Shrine ** Location: Motomiya Summit ({{Coord|33|08|45.56|N|131|35|34.34|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|name=Okumiya: Hongu Shrine}}) - About 2 hours one way from the main shrine grounds. *: This is the place where our company was founded. === Precinct Company === * Merged company * Itsukushima Shrine *Kiseisha * Isesha File:Gappei-sha (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Merger company File:Itsukushima-jinja (Sasamuta-jinja).JPG|Itsukushima Shrine === Main festivals === === Shikinen Festival === * '''Okamiso Festival'' (Kanmiso Festival) *: Special ritual. It is held on the day of the annual festival every 33rd year. The ceremony, which is the annual grand festival in which the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=divine clothing|1=UNKNOWN}} of the enshrined deity is newly made and presented, is based on the history book. . * '''Shinko Taisai'''' (Goshinko Festival) *: Held every third year. === Annual festival === *Monthly festival (1st day of every month) * New Year's Day Festival (January 1st) * Harvest Star Festival (February 1st-3rd) * Prayer Festival (March 15th) * Hongu Spring Festival (March 20th) * Annual festival (April 15th) * Fuji Festival (May 3rd-5th) *: The {{ill|lt=Fuji (plant)|Q1329209|WD=Q1329209|lt=Fuji|1=Wisteria floribunda}} flowers near Mannen Bridge are at their peak. Temple festivals, tree growing festivals, memorial services, water god festivals, and Kangaku festivals are held. * Great Purification (June 30th) * Summer festival (last Sunday of July) * Hongu Autumn Festival (October 20th) * Niinamesai (November 23rd) * Great Purification, New Year's Eve Festival, Komori Fuda Burning Festival (December 31st) === Cultural assets === === Cultural property designated by Oita Prefecture === * Mannenbashi Bridge (Tangible Cultural Property) - Designated on April 8, 1982. === Cultural property designated by Oita City === [[File:Sasamuta-jinja Fuji.JPG|thumb|right|Yama Fuji (city natural monument)]] * Jinko (tangible cultural property) - Designated on January 9, 1972. * {{ill|lt=Yamafuji|Q5783537|WD=Q5783537|1=Wisteria brachybotrys}} (natural monument) - Over 450 years old, tree height 3.5m, trunk circumference 2.8m[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1219359740812/index.html List of Oita City designated famous trees (tree section)] Oita City[https://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1166682381846/index.html Oita City designated famous trees No. 12, 13, 14] Oita City Children's Page. Designated on January 9, 1972 [http://www.city.oita.oita.jp/www/contents/1275373722750/index.html List of cultural properties designated by country, prefecture, and city] Oita City. It is also designated as a famous tree designated by Oita City (tree category). === Others === * Nishikanta Shrine Forest - Specially protected forest designated by Oita Prefecture, Oita City designated famous tree (forest section) [https://www.pref.oita.jp/soshiki/16210/hogojurin.html#8 List of specially protected forests] Oita Prefecture. === Transportation access === * Bus: Take the {{ill|lt=Oita Bus|Q11432629|WD=Q11432629|1=Oita Bus}} (bound for Fujigaoka) and get off at the "Fujigaoka Minami" bus stop. ({{Wiki coordinates|33|10|34.00|N|131|35|46.04|E|region:JP-44_type:landmark|location|name=Reference: Nearest bus stop "Fujigaoka Minami"}}, about 8 minutes walk after getting off) * Railway: {{ill|lt=Kyushu Railway|Q498366|WD=Q498366|lt=JR Kyushu|1=Kyushu Railway Company}}{{ill|lt=Hohi Main Line|Q870826|WD=Q870826|1=Hōhi Main Line}} {{ill|lt=Shikito Station|Q7496590|WD=Q7496590|1=Shikido Station}} (about 30 minutes walk) === Footnotes === === Notes === {{Reflist|group="Note"}} === Source === {{Reflist|2}} === References === * Shrine history book * "Japanese Historical Place Name System Oita Prefecture Place Names" ({{ill|lt=Heibonsha|Q11482108|WD=Q11482108|1=Heibonsha}}) Oita City Nishikanta Shrine section * Masahiro Hata "Nishikata Shrine" ({{ill|lt=Kenichi Tanigawa|Q2392596|WD=Q2392596|1=Ken'ichi Tanigawa}} ed. "Japanese Gods -Shrines and Sacred Sites- 1 Kyushu" ({{ill|lt=Hakusuisha|Q4346470|WD=Q4346470|1=Hakusuisha Publishing}})) * {{Cite book|Japanese book|editor=Edited by the Medieval Countries Ichinomiya System Study Group|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=Basic Research on the Ichinomiya System in Medieval Countries|publisher=Iwata Shoin|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|Medieval Countries Ichinomiya System|2000}}}} === Related books === * Motohiko Anzu and Yoshihiko Umeda editors and supervisors, "Shinto Dictionary", Jinja Shinposha, 1968, p. 31 * Edited by Eiji Shirai and Masanori Toki, "Dictionary of Shrines" {{ill|lt=Tokyodo Publishing|Q11524645|WD=Q11524645|1=Tōkyōdō Shuppan}}, 1979, p. 157 === Related items === * {{ill|lt=Yusihara Hachimangu Shrine|Q195715|WD=Q195715|1=Yusuhara Hachimangū}} - Bungo Province Ichinomiya Shrine confirmed in historical materials. *Nishikata Shrine - Shikinaisha ``Nishikata Shrine'' Ronsha. === External link === {{commonscat|Sasamuta-jinja}} * [https://sasamuta.com/ Nishikanta Shrine] Official website * [http://jmapps.ne.jp/kokugakuin/det.html?data_id=53425 Nishikanta Shrine] (Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program “Shinto/Shrine Historical Materials Collection”) {{Shinto horizontal}} {{Normdaten}} == Categories == [[Category:Wikidata generated shikinaisha pages|Sasamuta Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha|Sasamuta Shrine]][[Category:pages]][[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha]] [[Category:Shinto shrine]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Bungo Province]] [[Category:pages]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Ōita Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Oita, Oita]] [[Category:Buildings in Oita, Oita]] [[Category:式内大社]] [[Category:豊後国の式内社|大ささむたしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:大分県指定有形文化財]] [[Category:豊後国|社1]] [[Category:kkkkkkkkkkkkkk]] [[Category:nnnnnnnnn]] [[Category:qqqqqqq]]
